research_gaps: Absence of a systematic, up‑to‑date survey covering monocular depth estimation advances (2023‑2025) including transformer‑based encoders, self‑supervised video learning, and domain adaptation.
Lack of a unified benchmark suite that evaluates recent models on real‑time edge inference, illumination robustness, and cross‑domain generalization.
No consolidated taxonomy of loss functions, architectural modules, and dataset splits that links methodological choices to specific performance trade‑offs.

proposals.name: Comprehensive Survey & Benchmark Paper (CSB‑2025)
proposals.rationale: Compile all peer‑reviewed monocular depth works from 2023‑2025, categorize by architecture (CNN, ViT, hybrid), supervision regime (supervised, self‑supervised, semi‑supervised), and deployment constraints (real‑time, edge, cloud). Augment the survey with a standardized benchmark covering KITTI, NYU Depth V2, DynaDepth, and newly curated illumination‑varying and domain‑shift test sets.
proposals.expected_benefit: Provides the community a single reference point, accelerates literature navigation, and establishes baseline scores for future methods under consistent evaluation protocols.
proposals.risk: High authoring effort; risk of rapid obsolescence if new models appear after publication; requires coordination with dataset owners for test‑set releases.

proposals.name: Open‑Source Evaluation Hub (DepthEval‑Hub)
proposals.rationale: Develop a reproducible, containerized platform (Docker + CLI) that automatically downloads recent model checkpoints, runs them on the unified benchmark, and reports metrics (Abs Rel, RMSE, FPS, power). Include plug‑in support for future models and enable community contribution via GitHub.
proposals.expected_benefit: Ensures consistent, transparent performance reporting, lowers barrier for reproducibility, and facilitates rapid comparison of emerging methods.
proposals.risk: Maintenance overhead; potential incompatibility with proprietary codebases; requires sustained community engagement to keep the hub updated.

proposals.name: Meta‑Analysis of Real‑Time Edge Performance
proposals.rationale: Focus a short‑form systematic review on methods achieving >30 FPS on typical edge hardware (e.g., Jetson Nano, Snapdragon). Extract architectural tricks (quantization, pruning, efficient attention) and quantify trade‑offs between speed and accuracy across 2023‑2025 papers.
proposals.expected_benefit: Delivers actionable design guidelines for practitioners targeting embedded deployment, filling a niche not covered by broader surveys.
proposals.risk: Limited scope may overlook broader methodological insights; depends on availability of detailed runtime reports in original papers.
